title: Fontaine's Fine & Decorative Arts sale features over 100 Tiffany Studios works
summary: Fontaine’s Auction Gallery will present an important two-day Fine & Decorative Arts auction September 26-27 to include over 900 lots of Nineteenth-Twentieth Century lighting, Tiffany lamps, art glass, leaded glass windows, fine silver, porcelain, marble and bronze statuary, Asian items, paintings, pottery, American and European furniture, clocks and jewelry. Preview is by appointment only September 24-25. Bidding is available via Internet, phone and absentee. The auction includes such highlights as an early and rare Tiffany Studios "Dragonfly" table lamp, a Tiffany Studios "Oriental Poppy" table lamp and Park Avenue winter scene by Guy Wiggins. Represented in the sale will be items from the estate of Steve Hohener, two extensive painting collections and over 100 Tiffany Studios items, including examples of the Dragonfly, Nasturti

title: Gagosian presents major 60-year Brice Marden survey in New York
summary: Gagosian opened I Am Plane Image, a comprehensive survey of paintings by Brice Marden at the West 21st Street gallery in New York. Presented in collaboration with the Estate of Brice Marden, this is the first such exhibition of the artist’s work in the city in twenty years. Spanning six decades, the presentation includes major institutional loans from the Art Institute of Chicago, Whitney Museum of American Art, and others, as well as significant works from the Estate and notable private collections. It offers a historic opportunity to view works that have rarely, if ever, been exhibited before. In tandem, Gagosian, again in collaboration with the Estate, will publish Brice Marden: Catalogue Raisonné of Paintings, 1961–2023, edited by scholar Tiffany Bell. title: Ryuichi Sakamoto sound and time exhibition premieres at Hamburger Bahnhof
summary: “Ryuichi Sakamoto | seeing sound, hearing time” at Hamburger Bahnhof – Nationalgalerie der Gegenwart is the first major retrospective of the composer and artist in Europe. Ryuichi Sakamoto is regarded as a pioneer of electronic and experimental music who repeatedly redefined the boundaries between sound, film, performance and visual art. From the 2000s onwards, he developed three-dimensional sound environments, often in collaboration with international artists such as Shiro Takatani and Carsten Nicolai, or filmmaker Apichatpong Weerasethakul. “Ryuichi Sakamoto | seeing sound, hearing time” presents seven works in five large-scale installations and opens during Berlin Art Week. The exhibition centres on the intersection of sound and art, which has been a hallmark of Hamburger Bahnhof since it was founded 30 years ago. title: Guggenheim presents major Taryn Simon rotunda exhibition in New York
summary: The Guggenheim New York presents Taryn Simon | Father Country I Do Love You, a major exhibition premiering a new body of work by artist Taryn Simon (b. 1975, New York). On view during the 250th anniversary of the United States, this presentation will bring together never-before-seen photographs, texts, videos, and sculptures into a singular, interactive installation filling the entire rotunda. It marks the first monographic exhibition by a photography-based artist in the iconic spiral rotunda and the largest debut of new work ever staged at the Guggenheim. Nearly a decade in the making, Father Country I Do Love You (2026) traces the real life of one unnamed federal agent through 42 multipart artworks or “chapters.” The immense project is a labyrinth of stories in which Simon uncovers the ripple effects of her protagonist’s actions and inactions. title: Berlin museums launch Daniel Nikolaus Chodowiecki exhibition for 300th anniversary
summary: Daniel Nikolaus Chodowiecki was a superstar among Berlin artists in the late 18th century. To mark his 300th birthday, the Kupferstichkabinett, in cooperation with the Akademie der Künste and the Gemäldegalerie ‒ Staatliche Museen zu Berlin, is dedicating a cabinet exhibition to the artist, showcasing more than twenty of his most important works from all periods in his oeuvre. These works continue to inspire us with their subtle humour, but are also thought-provoking. Even now, the socio-political issues and Enlightenment subjects they touch upon and explore have not lost their relevance. Chodowiecki’s most significant works from around 1767, depictions of Der Abschied des Jean Calas von seiner Familie (The Parting of Jean Calas from His Family) ‒ from three collections ‒ can be viewed together for the first time at one location. title: Robin Williams, Stephen Colbert & 'South Park' comedy treasures up for Comic Relief 40th Anniversary Auction
summary: Julien’s Auctions and Comic Relief present the Comic Relief 40th Anniversary Auction, featuring comedy and entertainment memorabilia spanning four decades and a diverse range of cultural mediums. The collection features historic comedy props, signed scripts and recordings, original photography and portraiture, and cultural treasures extending beyond comedy, including a signed poster of 2026 NBA champion Jalen Brunson, comedian, actor, writer, and musician Steve Martin’s 2009 51st Annual Grammy Awards Nominee Medallion, and a signed prop violin from Jack Benny. Sourced from legendary talent, production teams, collectors, and enthusiasts, the auction reflects the breadth of the community that has supported Comic Relief throughout its 40-year history. title: Neue Nationalgalerie presents Maurizio Cattelan's first major German solo exhibition
summary: The Neue Nationalgalerie presents NIGHT, the first major solo exhibition in Germany by Italian artist Maurizio Cattelan, recipient of the Preis der Nationalgalerie 2026. Conceived for Mies van der Rohe’s glass hall, the exhibition brings together seminal historical works and new commissions in an installation that lends the museum the character of a contemporary church — a space of gathering, elevation and reflection. NIGHT takes shape around themes of history, power, memory, identity and belief. Across the exhibition, familiar images and figures are shifted just enough to unsettle their meaning, opening them to readings that move between irony and ambiguity. In dialogue with Mies van der Rohe’s architecture, Cattelan’s works activate the building not as a container, but as part of the exhibition itself. title: Open-top buses feature Design Ah! liveries in new M+ partnership
summary: M+, Asia's global museum of contemporary visual culture in the West Kowloon Cultural District (WestK) in Hong Kong, collaborates with The Kowloon Motor Bus Company (1933) Limited (KMB) to bring the popular Special Exhibition Design Ah! Experience the Wonder of Everyday Design beyond the museum and onto the streets of Kowloon. From now through November 2026, three Design Ah!-themed ‘KMB Tour HK’ ‘CITY CHARM’ HK1 Open-top Buses, featuring graphics that celebrates everyday actions will accompany the public throughout the bus journey. title: PICA announces Yona Lee as the 2027 Judy Wheeler Commission recipient
summary: Perth Institute of Contemporary Arts has today announced internationally acclaimed sculptor Yona Lee as the recipient of its 2027 Judy Wheeler Commission, a prestigious annual initiative championing the depth, diversity and bold innovation of Australian contemporary arts practice. Established in 2022, the 10-year program is made possible through a philanthropic gift to PICA by the Simpson Family in honour of their late wife and mother Judy Wheeler, a passionate supporter of the arts. Each year, the Judy Wheeler Commission supports the creation of a new site-specific work by an Australian artist that responds physically or conceptually to PICA’s building and its history, embodying the organisation’s spirit of experimentation and celebrating art’s power to connect people and places. For the 2027 Commission, Lee will create an expansive, site-specific sculpture that occupies PICA’s first floor and responds directly to its architecture. Constructed from stainless-steel

title: Panorama of Brazilian Art returns to MAM São Paulo featuring 33 contemporary artists
summary: The 39th Panorama of Brazilian Art: After It’s All Said, is on view at the Museum of Modern Art of São Paulo (MAM São Paulo) through January 24, 2027. Curated by Diane Lima, the exhibition marks MAM São Paulo’s return to its headquarters in Ibirapuera Park. One of Brazil’s most important exhibitions dedicated to contemporary artistic production, the 39th Panorama brings together 33 artists from 11 Brazilian states: Allan Weber, Amorí, Ana Claudia Almeida, André Felipe Cardoso, Anti Ribeiro, Arorá, Bárbara Banida, biarritzzz, Carolina Cordeiro, Caroline Ricca Lee, Chacha Barja, Darks Miranda, Emer Freire, Fykyá Pankararu, Gilson Plano, Helô Sanvoy, Iagor Peres, Josi, Jota Mombaça, Kuenan Mayu, Lia D Castro, Lita Cerqueira, Marcelo Conceição, Moacir Soares de Faria, nazas, Osvaldo Gaia, Oto Ferreira, Rafael Chavez, Rayana Rayo, Rodrigo Cass, Rose Afefé,

title: Sophie Delaporte pairs Needleworks series with early fashion photography in new show
summary: Sous Les Etoiles Gallery is presenting The Thread Between an exhibition by Sophie Delaporte bringing together her Needleworks series and a selection of her early fashion photographs. Spanning nearly three decades of artistic practice, the exhibition reveals a continuous exploration of femininity, desire, intimacy, and the representation of the female body. The exhibition will be on view through October 31st. The Thread Between evokes Delaporte’s way of challenging established visual codes from inside the image itself. Rather than rejecting the languages of fashion and erotic representation, she inhabits them, disrupts them, and ultimately makes them her own. Moving between photography, fashion, and physical intervention upon the image, Delaporte challenges conventional ways of looking. title: Andrew Jackson's Hermitage announces generational updates to the historic site and presidential home
summary: Andrew Jackson’s Hermitage is preparing for a once-in-a-generation transformation. The Andrew Jackson Foundation today announced plans for major improvements across the 1,120-acre historic site, including a new, approximately 70,000-square-foot Visitor and Education Center, expanded interpretation, restored historic spaces, new visitor amenities and a reimagined experience for the more than 170,000 people who visit The Hermitage each year. At the center of the broader vision is a simple idea: “Held by the Land.” The concept by renowned architect Perkins&Will places the historic landscape at the heart of the visitor experience. The proposed Visitor and Education Center will follow the natural contours of the property, with much of the building located below grade. A new, tree-lined approach and re-oriented walking paths will preserve important views while creating a stronger connection between visitors and the historic landscape. title: Tate celebrates a new generation with landmark commission for young artists
summary: Tate today marks a major milestone as Tate Collective, its free membership scheme for 16 to 25-year-olds, reaches a record 200,000 members, affirming its position as the world’s most popular arts membership scheme for young people. To celebrate, Tate has launched a landmark open call inviting Tate Collective members to create a new artwork for display in Tate Modern, the world’s most visited modern art museum. The selected artist will have their work shown on the gallery walls, alongside renowned figures including Andy Warhol, Salvador Dalí and Marina Abramović, offering an unparalleled platform for emerging talent. The only opportunity of its kind in London, this commission reflects Tate's continued commitment to championing young voices and creating pathways for the next generation of artists. Since 2018, Tate Collective’s ‘open calls’ have showcased the works of young artists around London and Liverpool.

title: Mohammed Sami is the National Gallery 2027 Artist in Residence
summary: The National Gallery today announced Mohammed Sami as its Artist in Residence for 2027. Celebrated for his powerful paintings of psychologically charged interiors and landscapes, Sami investigates both the possibilities and limits of painting as a means of evoking the memories of moments passed. His works often depict sites marked by conflict yet deliberately refrain from portraying acts of violence themselves. Instead, through nuanced painterly dexterity, he presents traces, fragments and remnants, constructing enigmatic scenes where the absence of human figures welcomes contemplation and interpretation. Sami has been invited to develop his artistic practice in dialogue with the National Gallery’s collection. Having begun his residency in August 2026, he will spend a year working in the Gallery’s onsite studio, with exceptional access to its collection

title: Kristen Lorello presents fifth solo exhibition with sculptor Bayne Peterson
summary: Kristen Lorello is presenting its fifth solo exhibition with Rhode Island-based sculptor Bayne Peterson. The exhibition features seven new hand formed pedestal-based sculptures in the artist’s iconic medium of laminated plywood, a medium the artist has been exploring since the gallery’s inception in 2014. Through luscious surfaces of sloping and concentric patterns, for more than a decade, Peterson has tested the optical and perceptual limits of hand formed three dimensional sculptures while refining his technical acuity in woodcarving. Labor, time, and the joy of process complement art historical and environmental research, resulting in sculptures that blend disparate themes and encourage the viewer to imagine beyond fixed categories. title: Armenian and German museums join forces for cross-collection exhibition in Yerevan
summary: To mark its 200th anniversary, the Museumsinsel Berlin is presenting itself for the first time in a cross-collection joint exhibition at the History Museum of Armenia in Yerevan. Under the title “Myths, Cult, Cosmology. Museumsinsel Berlin Visits Armenia,” approximately 50 selected objects from six collections of Museumsinsel Berlin engage in a dialogue with an equally large selection from the holdings of the Armenian partner museum. The roughly 100 exhibits open up new perspectives on myths, religious practices, and cosmological concepts of various cultures. In the fall of 2027, the collaboration will continue in Berlin: The Museumsinsel Berlin will then present a joint exhibition featuring significant archaeological treasures from Armenia. title: Alison Bradley Projects presents Yuki Tawada's first US solo exhibition
summary: Alison Bradley Projects is presenting Yuki Tawada, the artist’s first solo exhibition in the United States, featuring representative works from her oeuvre. The exhibition reveals Tawada’s sustained engagement with interrogating the myths of photographic objectivity while exploring the medium's potential. Through burning, piercing, cutting, transferring, and accumulating, Tawada challenges the photograph's assumed stability, treating the image as a material site where memory can be created, changed, released, and questioned. The exhibition coincides with Tawada’s inclusion in I’m So Happy You Are Here: Japanese Women Photographers from the 1950s to Now, a major retrospective of Japanese photography that gathers over 200 works by women artists from postwar Japan to today, on view this fall at the International Center

title: Burgundy auction raises nearly €800,000 for restoration of Cîteaux Abbey
summary: Organised by the Château du Clos de Vougeot and the Fondation du patrimoine, in partnership with Christie's, and in support of the restoration of the Définitoire of the Abbey of Cîteaux, Direct from Burgundy's Greatest Domaines pour l'Abbaye de Cîteaux | Acte II fundraising initiative concluded successfully on Saturday, 19 September. With a total of nearly €800,000 to be allocated to the restoration of this jewel of Burgundy's heritage, Clos de Vougeot for Abbaye de Cîteaux, Part II surpassed the results of the previous edition, which raised €650,000 in 2022. The restoration of the Définitoire will therefore benefit fully from the success of the 2026 edition, which comprised a charity dinner, auction organized by the Fondation du patrimoine and the Clos de Vougeot (along with other fundraising initiatives), held at the Château du Clos de Vougeot

title: Institution presents International Forum on the Sustainability of Culture 2026: Culture Commons
summary: Conceived as the first international forum dedicated specifically to the sustainability of culture, the event is a yearly large conference which brings together artists, thinkers, economists, researchers, and cultural professionals to address how culture can be sustained environmentally, socially, and economically. Following its first edition in 2025, the International Forum on the Sustainability of Culture returns on September 25–26, 2026 with Culture Commons, two days of discussions, lectures, and collective working sessions exploring culture as a shared infrastructure. The Forum asks what happens when the commons are considered not only as a theoretical framework, but as a practical model for cultural, economic, and social life. How can cultural resources, knowledge, technologies, and institutions be collectively governed and sustained?

title: Martos Gallery explores five decades of art by late iconoclast Dan Asher
summary: Adventurer/ethnographer, whether on the streets of the East Village or far afield—South America, Asia, Antarctica—a painter, photographer, sculptor, an obsessive draftsman, the artist Dan Asher (1947-2010) was a true force of nature. He possessed a restless energy, an elevated intelligence, well-read, well-traveled, always searching. An iconoclast, a mischief-maker, at times insistently impolite, the sort of figure today’s professionalized art world can’t easily accommodate, he slipped in and out of various scenes to which he was magnetically attracted. He could be alternately chaotic and hyper-focused, compulsive and meditative, all these dualities in the balance, and which also describe his art over five decades. title: Heidi Horten Collection presents major Elisabeth von Samsonow retrospective
summary: For the first time, this retrospective brings together nearly five decades of the artistic oeuvre of the German-Austrian artist and philosopher Elisabeth von Samsonow (b. 1956). Including many newly exhibited works, it presents the breadth of her practice alongside the philosophical thinking that has developed with it. Working across sculpture, painting, drawing, performance, and writing, and extending her practice into collective projects, Samsonow interweaves art, philosophy, feminist thought, pedagogy, and, increasingly, ecological engagement in a distinctive, vivid artistic language. Since Samsonow began working in wood in 1990, sculpture has been central to her practice. Carved from entire tree trunks, these works are life-size or larger; their painted surfaces broaden the sculptural form into the realm of painting. Samsonow’s sculptural vocabulary

title: Fondation Pernod Ricard releases major dual-language anthology celebrating 40 TextWork critical essays
summary: Since its inception in 2017, the TextWork programme has created a distinctive space for dialogue between writing and contemporary art practices. Developed by the Fondation Pernod Ricard with the support of the French Ministry of Culture, it is grounded in a shared ambition: to strengthen the international visibility of the French art scene by treating critical thought as a vital form of support for artists. TextWork brings together artists working in France and writers from abroad, fostering exchanges that result in substantial critical essays. More than an editorial project, it supports artists by offering sustained attention to their practices at a particular moment in their career. Today, the first 40 texts of the programme, presented in English and French, form the foundation of an expanding archive—a mirror of a scene in constant reinvention. Together,

title: U-Haul installation in Chelsea brings Nobuhira Narumi solo show to West 22nd Street
summary: The word for “moving” in Greek is “metaphora.” During three days, 20 U-Haul moving trucks will occupy West 22nd Street in Chelsea: a metaphor in action! For its first participation in the fair, Bienvenu Steinberg & C will present The Dog Run, the first U.S. solo presentation by Japanese artist Nobuhira Narumi. Narumi’s paintings begin with a simple question: what happens to the visible world when the human point of view is no longer its measure? The Dog Run starts with a passage toward a zone where the distinctions between body and environment, figure and ground, seeing and sensing begin to loosen. Drawing on his experiences with dogs and their owners across different countries and environments, Narumi turns familiar scenes into shifting fields of proximity, scent, memory, and attention. title: Nasher Sculpture Center presents Bruce Nauman's first Texas museum exhibition
summary: The Nasher Sculpture Center announces Bruce Nauman: Identical, an exhibition of recent sculptures and drawings depicting animal forms that build upon the artist’s long-term investigation of his own role as an artist and his daily practice in the studio. The show will be on view from September 19, 2026–March 21, 2027 and is Nauman’s first exhibition organized by a Texas museum. For over six decades, Bruce Nauman (American, b. 1941) has worked in a stunning range of media, from video, film, and sound, to neon, wax, and performance. His earliest works took his own body as subject matter, resulting in body casts and repetitive actions recorded on video.
